claim: A 32-bit RISC-V processor with a classic 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) was fully designed, implemented in Verilog, and functionally verified in ModelSim, demonstrating RISC-V processor design as a viable, documented ECE/electronic-systems final project.
stance_target: feasibility of RISC-V processor design as an ECE capstone/final-year project
scope_conditions: Master of Engineering in Electronic Systems dissertation, UTAR, Malaysia, Aug 2023
quoted_support: In this project, RISC-V processor is designed and simulated using Verilog... the designed RISC-V processor will be using 5-stage pipeline techniques to improve the overall performance of the processor.

claim: The processor's hazard unit implements both data forwarding (for register conflicts between EX/MEM and MEM/WB pipeline stages against ID/EX source registers) and pipeline stalling to resolve hazards forwarding alone cannot cover.
stance_target: hazard-handling mechanisms in the pipelined RISC-V implementation
quoted_support: forwardMuxA: Handle following 2 hazard conditions: 1. EX/MEM.RegisterRd = ID/EX.RegisterRs 2. MEM/WB.RegisterRd = ID/EX.RegisterRs

claim: The implemented RISC-V processor supports only the base integer instruction set and lacks floating-point, bit-manipulation, vector, and cryptography extensions, and it has no branch prediction, causing pipeline-flush penalties on every branch misprediction.
stance_target: feasibility scope and limitations of a base-ISA RISC-V final-project implementation
quoted_support: if the prediction is wrong, the processor had to flush the pipeline and fetch instructions from the correct branch, which causes a performance penalty.

claim: RISC-V is positioned in the dissertation as a free and open instruction set architecture (ISA) offering an alternative to proprietary CISC/RISC processor designs for both academic and industrial processor design work.
stance_target: RISC-V's value proposition relative to proprietary ISAs for academic project use
quoted_support: The design of RISC-V processor provides an alternative for software and hardware design to the computer designers as it provides free and open instruction set architecture (ISA).

claim: By 2030 more than 22.7 billion devices are projected to be connected via IoT networks, cited as motivation for VLSI/processor research relevance.
stance_target: IoT device growth projection motivating VLSI/embedded research
scope_conditions: cited from W. Wang et al., 2021, global projection to 2030
quoted_support: By 2030, more than 22.7 billion devices will be connected by IoT networks (W. Wang et al., 2021).
